correctness.rationale: The cubic contains no line meeting the dense torus because three affine-linear coordinate factors with product identically one must all be constant. For each rational chord, the cubic pullback factors t(t−1)(s3 t−s1), so a distinct rational third torus intersection exists exactly when s3, s1 and s1−s3 are nonzero. Counting the s3=0 subtori and the two disjoint tangent exclusion sets via rational parameter k gives tau=(q−2)(q−5)+2rho. Torus transitivity and incidence double-counting imply all four explicit n_j formulas, valid uniformly in every characteristic. The four distinct torus characters yield a dimension-four code; pairs of independent codewords correspond exactly to ambient rational projective lines. Hence d2 and optimal-subcode counts, plus d3,d4, follow. Direct all-projective-line censuses for q=3,4,5,7,8,9 and independent finite-field chord tests through q=27 reproduce the formulas. Finite checks corroborate but do not replace the universal proof.

originality.rationale: The novelty claim concerns the explicit complete 0,1,2,3 rational-line-intersection spectrum of the exceptional-triangle cubic, the cap-field dichotomy, and the exact second generalized weight and optimizer-subcode census for its four-dimensional toric evaluation code. Soprunov (2014) supplies the same natural four-monomial support but treats minimum distance; González Sarabia et al. (2016/2018) cover full projective torus codes with q-minus-one cubed points rather than this two-dimensional monomial torus with q-minus-one squared points; Patanker–Singh (2020) cover squarefree/hypersimplex supports. The implications of those results were compared and do not determine the claimed spectrum. Targeted published-source searches did not identify an equivalent full formula; a specialist finite-geometric line-spectrum result may still exist and is named as residual risk.

value.rationale: The exceptional lattice triangle is the canonical minimal strongly indecomposable four-lattice-point polygon, and its four-character toric evaluation code is motivated in primary literature. The exact generalized second weight and complete line-intersection spectrum are natural invariants not determined by the previously studied minimum-distance bounds. The result classifies all finite fields at the 2-MDS/cap threshold (orders 3 and 5), counts every optimal two-dimensional subcode, and proves a uniform geometric mechanism using cubic chords, a substantive classification rather than a trivial isolated or arbitrary parameter increment.
